body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Fatima Noor <fatima.noor@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jun 2, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Private Deployments: roadmap requests from regulated ABM conversations (triage for next 2 sprints)

Team — pulling together product feedback that’s come up repeatedly in regulated ABM conversations (finserv + healthcare). Goal: triage into (a) docs/enablement we can do now, (b) small product improvements we can pull into next 1–2 sprints, (c) roadmap items that need proper planning.

I’m trying to keep us disciplined: no major feature build for the pilot, but we do need crisp answers + a couple “paper cuts” fixes.

Top themes (from SE calls + questionnaires):

1) SAML/SSO edge cases (Private)
- Metadata validation failures w/ certain IdPs (customer showed “invalid entity descriptor”)
- Request to support multiple IdPs / multiple SSO connections per tenant (common in M&A)
- Signed assertions vs signed response requirements (varies by security policy)
- Attribute mapping: group -> role mapping, custom claim names, nameID formats

2) SCIM / provisioning (Private)
- “Do you support SCIM?” comes up almost every security review
- If not, they want a documented fallback workflow (JIT + RBAC + audit evidence)

3) Audit logs: export + schema clarity
- Need a concrete schema (fields + examples) and a supported export path
- Requests for: S3 delivery, Splunk/HEC, Azure Event Hub, syslog (varies)
- Must clarify what’s logged today vs “available on request” vs “not supported”

4) Retention controls (Hosted/Dedicated question spills over, but Private is where they expect control)
- “Can we set retention to 0 / disable persistence?”
- “Where is data stored? model inputs/outputs? logs?”

5) Private installer / deployment UX
- Preflight checks (GPU driver/CUDA, disk throughput, DNS, time sync, proxy)
- Better error messages + a single “requirements” checklist we can hand to IT
- Air-gapped install guidance (package mirrors, image signing/verif)

Ask:
- Naomi: please flag any claim-risk here (esp. around SCIM + audit exports) + what we can safely say in security reviews.
- Markus/Fatima: add specifics you’ve heard (exact asks, who asked, severity).
- Elliot/Kira: what’s the fastest docs path for “audit log export example” + SAML edge-case guidance.
- Lauren: if any of this bleeds into Dedicated packaging/positioning, call it out.

I attached a quick dump from my notes (sanitized) and one of the audit log export question PDFs.

Attachment(s):
- ABM-Regulated-Private-Feedback_2025-06-02.csv
- Brightline_AuditLog_Export_Questions.pdf
- Northbridge_SAML_Metadata_Error_Screenshot.png

If we can align by EOD Wed, I’ll convert into a short prioritized list + owners.

— Vivek

Product, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private Deployments: roadmap requests from regulated ABM conversations (triage for next 2 sprints)

A few immediate claim-risk flags:

- SCIM: We should not imply “SCIM supported” in outbound/security FAQ unless we have it GA and documented. Safe language is along the lines of: “SAML SSO supported; provisioning can be handled via customer IdP + Redwood RBAC; SCIM is on roadmap” (and only if asked).

- Audit log exports: We can say we provide audit logs and can export, but we need to be precise on *formats + mechanisms*. If we only have “pull via API / ship via customer-managed log pipeline,” we should avoid claiming “native Splunk integration” etc.

- Retention: We need to keep answers consistent with the regulated security FAQ. The risky zone is “we don’t store prompts” language — it depends on product + logging config. We should answer in terms of configurable retention for Private + what’s in-scope for logs.

Proposal: for this pilot, let’s create:
1) A one-page “SSO + provisioning” appendix (what we support + limitations)
2) A “Audit logs: fields + export patterns” appendix with sample payloads
3) A standard answer for “multiple IdPs” (even if it’s “one per tenant today; multi-IdP requires separate tenants” etc.)

I’ll sync w/ Aisha/Olga if we need GRC wording updates, but this looks mostly like product+docs.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Product Alignment | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private Deployments: roadmap requests from regulated ABM conversations (triage for next 2 sprints)

Adding color from the past ~3 weeks (ABM calls + pilots):

SAML
- Northbridge (pilot): IdP is Azure AD. They hit a metadata validation issue on first setup (ended up being a strict XML parsing expectation + cert chain mismatch). We opened SUP-51214 and worked around by re-exporting metadata with a different signing option.
- Regal Wealth deep dive: asked if we can enforce “signed assertions” and restrict accepted algorithms (they have a policy doc). Also asked about session duration controls.
- Multi-IdP request came up twice (one finserv, one healthcare) but both were “nice-to-have” vs blocker.

Audit logs
- Brightline security team explicitly asked for: who/what/when fields, admin actions (policy changes), auth events, and model invocation events. They want event IDs, correlation IDs, and ideally a “request_id” that matches app-side.
- They also asked about delivery: “can you stream to S3 hourly?” and “do you support Splunk HEC?” Our current answer got wobbly because we don’t have a single canonical export story.

Installer
- Cedarstone (on-prem constraints): asked for air-gapped install steps + a checklist of required outbound connections (if any) + how updates work.

None of these are “must build SCIM now” type requests, but we’re losing time in calls because the answers aren’t packaged.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference

+1 to Markus’s notes.

A couple more “frequently asked” items that might be low-effort improvements:

Audit log schema / content
- Prospects want clarity on whether prompts/completions appear in audit logs by default. Even if it’s configurable, we need an explicit statement.
- Many security teams specifically ask for a “data access” event (e.g., when an admin views logs, downloads evidence, changes retention). They treat it as SOX-ish control.

Export
- Even if we can’t build native integrations, having a supported “export to customer-owned S3 bucket” pattern (w/ IAM + encryption notes) would satisfy 70% of questions.

Installer
- The biggest pain: opaque failures on TLS certs / internal DNS / time drift. A simple preflight that checks NTP/time sync and cert validity would have prevented 2 escalations.

If it helps, I can compile the exact questions from Helix’s POC scoping call (they’re very process-heavy).

— Fatima

Docs path (fastest, minimal risk):

1) “Private: SSO & user management” page
- Supported: SAML 2.0
- Explicitly list tested IdPs (Okta/Azure AD) with “others may work” language
- Add a troubleshooting section for metadata parsing, cert chain, clock skew
- Call out current limitations (e.g., one IdP per tenant) clearly

2) “Audit logging in Private” page
- Define categories: auth events, admin/config changes, deployment events, inference request metadata (and explicitly whether payloads are included)
- Add examples: sample JSON event (redacted), list of fields

3) “Export patterns”
- If Engineering is aligned on a supported method, we can publish: file sink on the control plane + ship with Fluent Bit / Vector, or push to S3.
- We should avoid naming vendor-specific integrations unless they’re real.

We already have an engineering ticket to confirm the audit log fields/retention language (ENG-22091). If you sign off on the supported export “pattern,” Kira and I can draft this week and route for Naomi review.

Also: if the examples repo PR (audit log export example) is the canonical reference, we can cross-link it.

— Elliot

From a PMM standpoint, the biggest issue is inconsistency in what we promise during calls.

What would help immediately:
- A single “What we support today” section for SSO (SAML) + audit logs + retention
- A single “On the roadmap” list (SCIM, more export destinations) with *no dates*
- Suggested wording for the two common traps:
  1) “Do you store prompts/completions?” (answer depends on deployment/logging config)
  2) “Are you HIPAA-ready?” (we should keep it to security controls + customer responsibility; no blanket claims)

If we can package this into an internal one-pager + update the regulated security FAQ links, Sales will stop improvising.

— Soojin

This is super helpful. Proposed triage (focused on ABM pilot needs + high-leverage paper cuts):

NOW (this week; docs/enablement)
1) Internal one-pager: “Private in regulated environments: SSO + audit logs + retention”
- Owner: Soojin + Naomi (review)
- Inputs: Markus/Fatima for real questions + safe answers

2) Public docs updates (draft this week, publish after Security review)
- “Private: SSO & user management” incl. troubleshooting + limitations
- “Audit logging in Private” incl. field list + examples + whether payloads are included
- Owners: Elliot + Kira; Naomi as approver
- Dependency: confirm canonical audit log fields (ENG-22091)

3) Examples repo: audit log export pattern
- Owner: Kira to align w/ existing PR (redwood-examples/pr-318)
- Goal: a single supported “export pattern” we can point to in deep dives

NEXT (1–2 sprints; small product improvements)
4) SAML metadata validation hardening + clearer errors
- Tie to SUP-51214 learnings
- Add strictness toggles only if low-risk; otherwise better messaging + parsing

5) Installer preflight checks
- Focus: time sync/NTP, cert validity, DNS resolution, proxy detection
- Low engineering risk, high support reduction

LATER (roadmap; don’t promise)
6) SCIM provisioning
7) Multi-IdP per tenant
8) Native SIEM destination integrations (Splunk HEC/Event Hub/etc.)

Next steps:
- Elliot/Kira: please start the doc outline; I’ll add the exact “supported export pattern” language once Eng confirms.
- Markus/Fatima: send me 3–5 anonymized “verbatim” questions for the one-pager so we mirror how buyers ask.
- Naomi: please propose the exact safe phrasing for SCIM + log payloads + retention.

I’ll open/attach a small tracking ticket for the “NEXT” items so we don’t lose them after ABM.

— Vivek
